## Review checklist

- [ ] Hindi text uses Devanagari and reads naturally for the intended audience.
- [ ] Source intent, voice, and tone are preserved without word-for-word phrasing or added claims.
- [ ] Meaning, facts, warnings, and limitations are preserved.
- [ ] Suspected source errors or contradictions are flagged separately and not silently corrected.
- [ ] Each published translation has a notice linking to its repository provenance record, or target-project restrictions are documented and publication is held for human approval.
- [ ] Provenance records the source revision, source-check time, ISO 8601 UTC translation time, review status, and unresolved concerns; the page links to the repository commit permalink containing the record when available.
- [ ] English terms are useful in this context; unfamiliar terms are explained.
- [ ] The audience and relevant regional wording are noted.
- [ ] For adapted text, the source URL and reuse license are included.
- [ ] License text and required legal/attribution notices are preserved unchanged; only the README content is translated.
- [ ] If this is a Hinglish demonstration, it is clearly presented as a sample/proposal and does not claim the locale is accepted or standardized.
- [ ] High-impact technical claims have been flagged for specialist review.
- [ ] For upstream translations, I checked for overlapping issues or pull requests and used the target's required issue/branch workflow.
